$comment: Conservative seed of well-documented PUP/adware and browser-hijacker publishers, each with a short reason. Publisher names as they typically appear in Windows 'Programs and Features' / code-signing subject fields. No hashes: none are known with certainty. Extend cautiously; a wrong entry here is a false-positive on a real vendor.

publishers.reason: Publishes a long history of bundled browser toolbars and search hijackers (e.g. Ask Toolbar-era products) widely flagged as PUP by antivirus engines.
Ask Partner Network; historically the distribution arm behind the Ask Toolbar bundled with third-party installers and flagged as a browser hijacker.
Publishes registry cleaner, driver-updater and 'PC optimizer' titles frequently flagged as PUP for scareware-style upselling.
Adware company behind the Superfish visual-search software that injected ads and installed a trusted root certificate; widely flagged as adware/PUP.
Toolbar and 'SearchProtect' browser-hijacker platform bundled with many free downloads; widely flagged as PUP.
Ad-injection browser extension/adware bundled with free software installers; widely flagged as adware.
